title: Kartids
capsule: The Kart dynasty was a Sunni Muslim ruling house of Ghurid origin that governed the Herat region of present-day Afghanistan from 1245, when the Mongol Ilkhanate confirmed Shams al-Din Kurt as governor of the city in return for submission. The Kartids flourished as cultural patrons under the Ilkhanate umbrella, particularly under Ghiyath al-Din (r. 1307–1329), commissioning major architectural works in Herat and effectively acting as autonomous rulers after Ilkhanid power weakened in the 1330s. Mu'izz al-Din Husayn (r. 1332–1370) formally ended Ilkhanid suzerainty and briefly conquered much of Khorasan before Timur (Tamerlane) captured Herat in 1381, executing the last Kart ruler Ghiyath al-Din Pir Ali and extinguishing the dynasty.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The Kartid realm centred on Herat is well attested in Persian chronicles, but the extent of frontier dependencies in Sistan and Ghazni fluctuated and is only roughly reconstructed from narrative sources.
